newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-AIKMAN LEADS COWBOYS PAST DOLPHINS AND FORMER COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-AIKMAN LEADS COWBOYS PAST DOLPHINS AND FORMER COACH.

text.p: It was the most hotly-anticipated game of the season, and when it was over the Dallas Cowboys had played like Super Bowl champions against the coach who led them to the first two their three titles of the 1990s.
Troy Aikman threw for 363 yards and three second-half touchdown passes and Dallas bottled up Miami's offence after halftime as the Cowboys handed Jimmy Johnson's Dolphins a resounding 29-10 defeat.
Aikman overcame a 10-9 halftime deficit by directing Dallas to 19 unanswered points in the first meeting between the Cowboys and Johnson.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones fired Johnson in 1994 over a clash of gigantic egos after he led the team to consecutive Super Bowl wins. Johnson returned to coaching this season.
"This was a special game for me, I admit it," Johnson said. "I'm disappointed, but we'll meet again."
Michael Irvin had 12 catches for 186 yards and one touchdown as Dallas improved to 5-3.
Star quarterback Dan Marino returned to the Miami lineup but could not prevent his team from losing for the fourth time in their last five games to fall to 4-4.
At Arizona, Adrian Murrell rushed for a 199 yards and a touchdown as the New York Jets finally won a game, beating the Cardinals 31-21.
Murrell carried 31 times and capped a 90-yard drive with a one-yard TD plunge in the fourth quarter as the Jets (1-8) ended a 12-game losing streak dating back to last November 26.
Keyshawn Johnson, who guaranteed the Jets would not finish 0-16, did his part by catching a 34-yard touchdown pass from Frank Reich in the second quarter.
"When the last ball was caught everyone relaxed. It's just great," said much-relieved Jets coach Rich Kotite.
That left the Falcons the only winless team in the NFL.
In Atlanta, Norm Johnson kicked a 20-yard field goal with three seconds remaining to lift the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) to a 20-17 victory that dropped the woeful Falcons to 0-8.
The Falcons tied the game on Bobby Hebert's touchdown pass to Bert Emanuel with 5:55 to play, but the Steelers drove 66 yards in 13 plays to set up Johnson's winning kick.
In Washington, Terry Allen rushed for 124 yards and three touchdowns to lead the surprising Redskins to their seventh win in row, a 31-16 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
It was the second consecutive three-touchdown game for Allen, who leads the NFL with 13.
Washington (7-1) is off to its best start since opening with 11 wins in 1991 en route to a Super Bowl title. The Colts (5-3) lost for the third time in four games.
In Houston, Jeff Brohm replaced an injured Steve Young and hit Terrell Owens with a 20-yard scoring pass with 4:27 left to lift the San Francisco 49ers to a 10-9 win over the Oilers.
Young suffered a concussion on San Francisco's first series and did not return. Brohm was in because regular backup Elvis Grbac suffered a separated left shoulder last week.
The win moved the Niners (6-2) into sole possession of first-place in the NFC West.
In Denver, John Elway threw for 286 yards and three touchdowns as the Broncos avenged their only loss of the season with a 34-7 rout of the Kansas City Chiefs.
Elway completed 16-of-31 passes, doing most of his damage in the first half when the Broncos (7-1) opened a 24-7 lead. In his last four games, Elway is 96-of-153 for 1,290 yards and 12 touchdowns.
Tight end Shannon Sharpe had two first-quarter touchdown catches and finished with six receptions for 99 yards.
In Green Bay, Dorsey Levens scored a second-quarter touchdown and Chris Jacke booted a pair of first-half field goals as the Packers beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 13-7.
But Green Bay (7-1) lost leading receiver Antonio Freeman for 4-6 weeks with a broken arm. The Packers had already lost top receiver Robert Brooks for the season two weeks ago.
Packers' star quarterback Brett Favre failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time in 17 games.
At Detroit, New York intercepted Lions quarterback Scott Mitchell three times in the second quarter and exploded for 23 points in a 4:54 span as the Giants clobbered Detroit 35-7.
Chris Calloway and Thomas Lewis caught second-quarter touchdown passes for the Giants, who also returned two interceptions for touchdowns.
"It's a lot more fun to receive seven turnovers rather than give them," said Giants coach Dan Reeves.
In Philadelphia, rookie tight end Jason Dunn caught his first touchdown pass and Rickey Watters added a scoring run as the Eagles (6-2) beat the Carolina Panthers 20-9.
Ty Detmer completed 23-of-38 passes for 342 yards, including seven for 143 yards to Irving Fryar, who became the 15th player in NFL history to record 600 career catches.
In Baltimore, Vinny Testaverde tossed a 22-yard touchdown pass to Michael Jackson with 10 seconds left in overtime to lift the Ravens to a 37-31 victory over the St Louis Rams.
The Rams (2-6) tried a 33-yard field goal with 5:49 left in overtime but holder Jamie Martin couldn't handle the snap.
The Ravens (3-5) had a chance to win in regulation but Matt Stover hooked a 39-yard field goal try as time expired.

In Cincinnati, Ki-Jana Carter had a pair of touchdown runs under three minutes apart in the fourth quarter as the Bengals rallied for a 28-21 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars for new coach Bruce Coslet.
Jeff Blake was 19-of-30 for 244 yards and two touchdown passes for the (2-6) Bengals.
In Seattle, Chris Warren rushed for 146 yards and a touchdown and Darryl Williams returned an interception 79-yards for a score as the Seahawks upended the San Diego Chargers 32-13.
Todd Petersen kicked four field goals for the Seahawks (3-5), who had a big defensive game with four interceptions, four sacks and a fumble recovery.

At New England, Curtis Martin's 10-yard touchdown run with 85 seconds left gave the Patriots the lead and Willie McGinest's 46-yard interception return for a score sealed a 28-25 victory over the Buffalo Bills.
The victory moved New England (5-3) into a first-place tie with the Bills and the Indianapolis Colts in the AFC East.
Buffalo quarterback Jim Kelly completed a 48-yard desperation touchdown pass to Andre Reed with 24 seconds, but the Bills were unable to recover the ensuing onside kick.
Kelly is suffering a nightmarish season with 12 interceptions and just four touchdown passes.
